title: Endovascular Treatment for Stroke Due to Occlusion of Medium or Distal Vessels
shortTitle: DISTAL: no disability benefit from routine distal-vessel thrombectomy
summary: DISTAL randomized 543 patients with selected medium/distal intracranial occlusions to EVT plus medical care or medical care alone within 24 hours. Ninety-day disability did not improve (common OR 0.90; 95% CI 0.67–1.22; P=.50). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 5.9% versus 2.6%.
whyItMatters: Do not extend the established benefit of large-vessel thrombectomy automatically to these distal occlusions. Continue urgent stroke assessment and eligible medical reperfusion treatment.
limitations: Median NIHSS was 6 and eligible occlusion locations were specified, including nondominant/codominant M2. Results do not settle every vessel, severity or device subgroup.
population: Patients with isolated eligible MCA, ACA or PCA medium/distal occlusions.
primaryEndpoint: Distribution of modified Rankin Scale scores at 90 days.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill. Primary PubMed abstract and electronic date reviewed; full text was not reviewed. PubMed labels this a free article and links a legal University of Liege repository copy. Do not infer full-text appraisal from availability.
